blockAssessments.assessment: Paragraph 1 retains identical finite facing parallel metal plates, lateral dimensions much greater than separation, no-fringing uniform-field approximation, facing area S for each plate, and separation d. Paragraph 2 retains equal opposite free plate charges, a linear homogeneous isotropic dielectric completely filling the gap, electrostatic equilibrium, and |q| used to express |U|. Paragraph 3 faithfully carries field, separation, charge, and medium dependence. The extra paragraph break changes no condition.

The one-plate field E1 and original formula reference are retained. Equal field magnitudes and common direction from positive to negative plate are scoped to the stated approximation and to the space between the plates; superposition is not asserted as an exact finite-plate field everywhere.

Dimensionless relative permittivity remains distinct from dimensional vacuum permittivity. The SI expression E=2E1=|sigma|/(epsilon epsilon0) is unchanged and is read under the complete model assumptions.
Signed q is the free charge of one plate, sigma=q/S is its surface charge density, and the other plate has equal magnitude and opposite sign. This is not total capacitor net charge.
The field-magnitude formula retains |q|, epsilon0, epsilon, and S exactly, including the approved mathematical atom order.

The potential-difference heading and text faithfully retain the uniform-field approximation, crossing the separation in the field direction, and magnitude of potential difference equal to field magnitude times distance.
Formula (8-37) remains |U|=Ed=|q|d/(epsilon0 epsilon S), with both charge and potential difference treated as magnitudes.

Nonzero-charge cancellation precedes the SI result. Fixed geometry, separation, medium properties, external-conductor conditions, and measurement connections qualify charge-independent capacitance. The zero-charge limit is the same linear ratio, not an evaluation of 0/0.
Formula (8-38), C=epsilon0 epsilon S/d, and its SI context are retained exactly. No new geometry or measured coefficient is introduced.

Paragraph 12 keeps CGSE charge, potential, and length units distinct from SI, rejects setting dimensional SI vacuum permittivity equal to a dimensionless constant, and forbids unit mixing. Paragraph 13 introduces the electrostatic-system formula without changing that scope.
Formula (8-39), C=epsilon S/(4 pi d), is unchanged and remains in the explicitly separate CGSE context.

Paragraph 15 retains the qualitative adjustable-separation capacitor/electrometer demonstration and the grounded casing and rod connections to different plates. Paragraph 16 retains charging by a separate charged rod, ending charging, removing that rod, neglecting leakage from the insulated plate, and approximately fixed free charge. Paragraph 17 keeps area and medium unchanged and controls measurement connections, nearby objects, and fringing; increasing |U| at the same plate charge signifies lower C. Paragraph 18 explicitly limits the observation to a qualitative trend, not a measured coefficient or universal exact result. 'Electrometer rod' faithfully identifies the source's shaft connection; it is not a persistent charging rod.

The empty prose slot, fig-152 identity, inherited machine label, printed page, and source reference remain unchanged. Only applicability of the surrounding English to the existing approved apparatus is accepted here; no source, geometry, current pixel, width, or accessibility verdict is issued.

The visible English caption translates the approved source caption faithfully. Its inherited machine label and source identity remain unchanged. It adds no material, measurement, electrical connection, or scientific claim.

Paragraph 19 carries forward the stopped-charging/no-leakage comparison, inserts an acrylic dielectric slab, and holds separation and facing area fixed as voltage decreases and capacitance increases. Paragraph 20 expressly says insertion does not establish full-gap filling. Paragraph 21 permits direct use of the simple formulas only for full filling by a linear homogeneous isotropic dielectric and the valid uniform-field approximation. No exact partial-insertion multiplier is claimed.

Paragraph 22 limits small d and large S/relative permittivity to maintained insulation and the uniform-field approximation, and retains the dimensionless permittivity definition. Paragraph 23 retains the book-sized capacitor comparison as a possibility and scopes Earth's capacitance to the isolated conducting sphere in vacuum estimate, not a universal measurement. Paragraph 24 distinguishes large equal opposite plate charges at small potential difference from large whole-capacitor net charge.

Paragraph 25 preserves the distinction between raising C at a given voltage and raising voltage at fixed C; it does not deny charge-voltage dependence. Excessive field can destroy dielectric insulation and cause conduction. Paragraph 26 explicitly states that breakdown invalidates the assumed linear insulating-medium model and may damage the capacitor.

conditionChecklist.condition: Identical finite facing parallel plates, facing area S, separation d, lateral size much greater than d.
Linear homogeneous isotropic dielectric fully fills the model gap; uniform field and neglected fringing.
Signed single-plate free charge and opposite plate charge distinguished from |q|, |U|, and field magnitudes.
SI and CGSE units remain distinct; dimensional epsilon0 is not replaced by a dimensionless constant.
Capacitance is charge independent only with the fixed linear model and unchanged external/measurement conditions; nonzero cancellation and zero limit remain scoped.
Charging ended, charging rod removed, leakage neglected, insulated plate free charge approximately fixed.
Separation-change observation is qualitative and controls area, medium, connections, nearby objects, and edge effects.
Partial acrylic insertion is not assumed to fill the full gap or establish the exact full-fill coefficient.
Earth comparison is scoped to an isolated-sphere estimate in vacuum.
Large equal/opposite plate charges are not large net capacitor charge; voltage still matters at fixed C.
Breakdown invalidates the linear insulating model; no unlimited small-gap/high-voltage conclusion.
